item.title: [7.0] Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Unified multimodal models (UMMs) integrate image generation and visual understanding, but are existing single-pathway unlearning methods sufficient to suppress target concepts across both? In this work, we study cross-pathway concept unlearning. Our goal is to prevent a model from both generating images of a target concept and identifying it in input images, while preserving other capabilities.

WHY IT MATTERS

This paper addresses an emerging challenge in machine unlearning for unified multimodal models, introducing a new benchmark and method (UniForget) for cross-pathway concept suppression.

item.title: [6.9] Advances in Agentic Computer Graphics
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Computer graphics is built on code. Large language model (LLM) agents can now generate graphics code and iteratively refine it through various feedback. This capability opens the door to a potentially new paradigm of computer graphics, with graphics algorithms increasingly built around agentic systems to automate progressively complex tasks.

WHY IT MATTERS

This report provides a valuable unified taxonomy and literature system for the rapidly growing field of agentic computer graphics, helping to organize fragmented research.
